guarantees.claim: cfg_block is set to 1 when hash_start_or_continue is asserted, regardless of reg_hash_done or reg_hash_stop.
cfg_block is cleared to 0 when reg_hash_done or reg_hash_stop is asserted, provided hash_start_or_continue is not asserted.
cfg_block retains its previous value when none of the explicit update conditions are met (no else clause).

assumptions.claim: hash_start_or_continue is a pulse, not a persistent level, so that cfg_block is not permanently stuck at 1.
assumptions.cond: when hash operation ends and reg_hash_done/reg_hash_stop are expected to clear cfg_block
assumptions.risk: Continuous assertion of hash_start_or_continue overrides done/stop, causing cfg_block to stay high, potentially locking the hash engine and preventing new operations.

assumptions.claim: reg_hash_done and reg_hash_stop are asserted only when cfg_block is 1 and not simultaneously with hash_start_or_continue.
assumptions.risk: Asserting done/stop while start is active leads to priority-driven set (cfg_block stays 1) potentially ignoring a legitimate end-of-operation event.

uncertain_points.claim: Simultaneous assertion of hash_start_or_continue and (reg_hash_done or reg_hash_stop) sets cfg_block to 1, ignoring the done/stop. Is this prioritization intended?
uncertain_points.risk: If the design requires that done/stop always clears cfg_block even during a new start request, a stuck busy state could occur, blocking subsequent hash operations.

uncertain_points.claim: No watchdog or timeout mechanism within this chunk clears cfg_block if reg_hash_done/reg_hash_stop never assert (e.g., due to internal error).
uncertain_points.cond: hash operation hangs or completes without status flags
uncertain_points.risk: cfg_block remains 1 indefinitely, potentially rendering the HMAC configuration interface inoperable until reset (denial of service).
